Having visited countless seafood restaurants across Goa, the Konkan region, and Mumbai, I can confidently say that Jai Hind tops my list.

Yes, there’s almost always a long waiting line, and at times you may be asked to share a table with other diners. But honestly, that’s only because the place is packed with people who keep coming back for the food. And once you taste it, you’ll understand why.

The seafood is fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. What makes the experience even better is the value for money. Unlike many places that charge extra for every little thing, the thali here is genuinely generous and unlimited, you can ask for refills of the items in your thali as many times as you’d like.

Great food, excellent portions, and prices that feel justified. If you’re a seafood lover, the wait is absolutely worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Liviu-Alexandru Buftea (Style)
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you found this place, you had a good guide!

I thought it was Portuguese, but it's actually British. Black as the basaltic rock that rises from the sea, Worli Fort gives a great overview of the bay and the city. It features the classic crenelations and ramparts of the 17th century, and guards the golf from the tip of this tongue of land.

The fort now is not officially maintained or "open to the public". In fact, it seems even locals don’t know about it, but my friend brought me here cause she heard it’s nice. It is accessible for explorer types, and is basically left abandoned.

The fort is simply used by people in this neighborhood for storage, hang out, kids play space, etc. Some clothes left out to dry on the sides, and some barrels and stuff in the rooms below.

Here we met a couple of guys from the city, chilling, listening to cool music, they welcomed us to chat.

It smelled of sea salt, soap, garbage, fish and rats, and the breeze brought “fresh” air from the sea.

As a first time visitor in India, I was in culture shock. Seeing everything was kind of like a dreamy, surreal landscape. So I probably romanticized it too much, for the place is a slum surrounded by a garbage dump, and people here have little chance to better their days, but they were happy, kind and curious.

It was an interesting and humbling experience, worth respect.

Please note, this restaurant has no washroom so if you are visiting with children and elderly relatives/people, keep this in mind.

featured_reviews.name: Prasad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Chaitanya for the second time, and it’s still one of the best places for authentic Konkan Malvani food in Dadar, Mumbai. Truly one of the rare restaurants that serves genuinely authentic seafood
Chaitanya easily ranks at the top!
The place is always crowded, so be prepared to wait outside for at least 20–40 minutes. The seating area is small, but the food makes it completely worth the wait. Prices depend on the current fish rates.
We tried the special prawns thali, which comes with double portions of prawns fry absolutely delicious. Also had the surmai thali with two fried pieces, and the taste was awesome. The bhakri was soft and fresh.
The best part was the unlimited solkadi, along with tasty crab lollipop. Service was quick too—food arrived within 5–10 minutes. Highly recommended for seafood lovers!

Thank you for your review! We’re delighted you enjoyed the authentic Malvani flavours, especially the thalis, crab lollipop, and unlimited solkadhi. Your patience with the wait truly means a lot to us—we look forward to welcoming you again soon!
Team Chaitanya

It was amazing to be and meet the roots always. If you miss Assal malvani food. This place will complete your cravings.

Its good restaurant for family, friends and couples as well. Service top notch, food top notch and worth each penny you will spend.

Vishnu hosted us, and took care all the needs during we were there. He knows all the foods so well and suggest nicely.

We have bombil fry(Bombay Duck) do not miss this one. Then we took mutton thali in that u will get nicely cooked mutton and the malvani gravy of mutton was awesome. Along with that there was kaleji masala (liver gravy) one more fantastic preparation  of assal malvani food. Don't miss having it with kombdi wade(its made of traditional flour mixed and fried nice and fluffy) or ghavne (Rice flour). Along with this all, they will also serve Solkadi (its a drink made of nice blend of wild mangosteen fruits along with some garlic and coriander, its amazing drink) do not miss this.

And to conclued this tasty food have parole (made of Rice flour and grated coconut,sweetened by jaggery with lot of ghee)

You must visit to this place and do try the amazing food of Indian west costline. This place will not disappoint you at all..

Thank you so much for the review! We’re truly glad our Malvani flavours, food recommendations, and Vishnu’s hospitality made your visit memorable. Looking forward to welcoming you back again for another authentic coastal feast.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ A Hidden Gem for Seafood Lovers!
If you are craving an authentic, soul-satisfying fish thali, Sarang is the absolute place to be.
The Food: Simply excellent. Every component of the thali—from the perfectly fried stuffed Pomfret with its crisp coating to the rich, flavorful coastal curry—tastes incredibly fresh and expertly spiced. It’s the kind of food that leaves you entirely satisfied yet already planning your next visit.
The Ambiance: The restaurant is small and cozy, but that’s exactly what gives it its charm. It has a genuinely warm, homely vibe that makes you feel instantly welcome, as if you're dining at a close friend's house.
Service & Staff: The service here is top-notch. The staff is exceptionally polite, courteous, and attentive, ensuring you have everything you need without ever feeling intrusive.
The Verdict: Incredible value for money! For the quality and quantity of food they serve, it is not expensive at all.
Highly recommended if you want spectacular coastal flavors paired with heartwarming hospitality. I will definitely be back for more!
